t:
Paragraph (13) of section 8(b) of the Small Business Act is amended to read as follows:


“(13) 
to establish such advisory boards and committees as may be necessary to achieve the purposes of this Act and of the Small Business Investment Act of 1958; to call meetings of such boards and committees from time to time; to pay the transportation expenses and a per diem allowance in accordance with section 5703 of title 5, United States Code, to the members of such boards and committees for travel and subsistence expenses incurred at the request of the Administration in connection with travel to points more than fifty miles distant from the homes of such members in attending the meetings of such boards and committees; and to rent temporarily, within the District of Columbia or elsewhere, such hotel or other accommodations as are needed to facilitate the conduct of such meetings; and”.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the section does not say who sits on these boards, so they could be internal federal bodies, and that the text is only about travel reimbursement. That fails because the provision authorizes the Administration to establish advisory boards and committees, call their meetings, and pay per diem and travel expenses for members coming from their homes more than fifty miles away. Those payment terms (section 5703 covers intermittent or uncompensated service) indicate the members are outside individuals rather than regular federal employees. Advisory committees with non-federal members advising the agency count as participation, even when establishing them is discretionary.
fable.s: to establish such advisory boards and committees as may be necessary to achieve the purposes of this Act and of the Small Business Investment Act of 1958; to call meetings of such boards and committees from time to time

qwen_block.w: The section authorizes the establishment of advisory boards and committees. The provision for paying 'per diem allowance' and transportation expenses to members indicates that these are likely non-federal participants (outside experts or stakeholders) rather than federal employees, who would typically be paid salaries. Advisory boards with outside members constitute participation.
qwen_block.s: to establish such advisory boards and committees as may be necessary to achieve the purposes of this Act... to pay the transportation expenses and a per diem allowance... to the members of such boards and committees

opus.w: The section lets the Small Business Administration create advisory boards and committees and call their meetings, which gives advisers a role in carrying out the Small Business Act. Members get per diem and travel pay for trips from their homes, which suggests they are outsiders rather than federal employees, as in Example 8. The tempting reading treats this as purely internal logistics, but advisory bodies with outside members are participation.
opus.s: to establish such advisory boards and committees as may be necessary to achieve the purposes of this Act and of the Small Business Investment Act of 1958; to call meetings of such boards and committees from time to time; to pay the transportation expenses and a per diem allowance in accordance with section 5703 of title 5, United States Code, to the members of such boards and committees
opus.b:
**Tempting wrong reading:** The section mostly covers logistics: paying travel expenses, per diem and hotel rentals. It also never names who sits on the boards, so it could look like internal administration with no outside party.

**Why that fails:** The provision authorizes the Small Business Administration to set up advisory boards and committees to help carry out its statutes. It pays members' travel "from the homes of such members" and a per diem allowance under 5 U.S.C. 5703. That pattern points to members from outside the government, as in Example 8. Advisory boards with outside members are participation under the definition.

qwen_chat.w: The section authorizes the establishment of advisory boards and committees and specifies that members receive per diem allowances and transportation expenses for attending meetings. This payment structure is typical for non-federal experts or outside appointees, rather than federal employees who receive salaries. Therefore, these boards likely include people outside the federal government, satisfying the definition of participation.
qwen_chat.s: to pay the transportation expenses and a per diem allowance in accordance with section 5703 of title 5, United States Code, to the members of such boards and committees for travel and subsistence expenses incurred at the request of the Administration in connection with travel to points more than fifty miles distant from the homes of such members in attending the meetings of such boards and committees
qwen_chat.b:
Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the text mentions "advisory boards and committees," it automatically constitutes participation. However, the definition requires that these bodies include non-federal members. If the boards were composed entirely of federal employees, it would be "No." The key here is the payment structure.

Resolution: The text specifies that members receive "transportation expenses and a per diem allowance... for travel and subsistence expenses." Federal employees are typically paid salaries and reimbursed for travel under different statutory authorities, whereas per diem allowances for attendance at meetings are characteristic of outside experts or non-federal appointees serving on advisory committees. This implies the boards include people outside the federal government.
